_help: The Privacy page. Plain-English draft: have a lawyer check it before taking payments. Keep it matching what the site really collects. Lines starting with TODO are placeholders.
title: Privacy policy
intro: web3.toys is built so you can play without telling us anything. This page lists exactly what we collect, why, who helps us store it, and how to delete it.

sections.title: If you just play
list: Your progress, coins, certificates and tool inputs are saved in your own browser (local storage). They are not sent to us.
Tools run in your browser. What you type into a tool is not sent anywhere.

We count simple page events (a toy was opened, started, finished or shared) without your name, to see which toys people like. If a page breaks, we record the error message (cut short, with emails and long numbers removed) and, for one visit in five, how long the page took to load. None of this includes who you are.
Small extras are kept in your browser too: your Hall of Famers wall, which toys you asked to be told about, and whether you hid the coin button. Clearing your browser data removes them.
When you answer a Web3 Hall of Famers clue, we add one to a total of how many players named that person. Only the total is stored, never who answered.

sections.title: If you create an account
list: Your login: your email address, or your X or Google account id, plus the name and profile picture that service shares with us. We never get your password.
When and which version of this policy you agreed to.
Your progress: toys played, scores, certificates, Pro tags, rank, coins and cosmetic extras, so you can see them on any device and on the leaderboard.

You get a random cartoon picture and a random fun display name (like SleepyFrog42). We do not show your real name or your X or Google picture. The leaderboard shows only your display name, picture, rank and coins. You can change your name or get a new picture any time.
If you join through someone's invite link, we store who invited you, so both of you can get the invite bonus. If you claim the X post task, we keep the link to your post so we can check it.
Early Bird: if you are one of the first players to earn a toy's certificate, we store your spot number for that toy (for example Early Bird #87) and the double coins it gives.
If you vote for a favourite builder in Web3 Hall of Famers, we store your one vote so it can be changed and counted. Only vote totals are shown.

sections.title: If you buy something
list: What you bought, the price, the date and the payment reference, so we can give you your download and a receipt.
Card and UPI payments are handled by Razorpay. Your card, UPI or bank details go to Razorpay, not to us. Razorpay's own privacy policy applies to them.
Crypto payments are handled by Paymento. You pay from your own wallet; we see the order and its status, and like every blockchain payment, the transaction is public on the blockchain.
Calls booked through Cal.com are handled by Cal.com and its payment provider.

sections.title: If you tap Notify me
list: We store your email address (or your account's email if you are logged in), the toy you want to hear about and the time you agreed.
We use it only to email you about that toy's launch: the day before and on launch morning. Every email has an unsubscribe link, and you can ask us to remove you at any time.

sections.title: If you join the email list, write to us or send a request
list: Your email address and the page you signed up from, to send you the updates you asked for. Every email has an unsubscribe link.

For project requests: your name and role, email, project name, website, X handle, Telegram username, the Telegram group link you choose to share, your answers, and payment and review status, to review your project, talk to you and deliver your request.
If you use the Contact form, we keep your name, email, topic and message so we can reply. We keep it only as long as we need to help you and keep a record of what we answered.
If you ask for a refund from My Progress, we keep your reason with the order so we can handle it.

sections.title: Who helps us
list: Supabase (accounts, database and private file storage).
Vercel (hosting the website).
Razorpay (card and UPI payments, and receipts).
Paymento (crypto payments).
Cal.com (booking calls).
Our email providers: Supabase for login links, and Resend for receipts and launch emails.
We do not sell your data and we do not use advertising trackers.

sections.title: How long we keep it
list: Account and progress data: until you delete your account.
Purchase records: as long as the law requires us to keep financial records, even after you delete your account.
Email list: until you unsubscribe.
Notify me emails: until the toy has launched and both emails are sent, then removed within 90 days, or sooner if you ask.
Project requests: for as long as your project is with us, and financial records as the law requires.

sections.title: Deleting your data
list: Logged in: open My account and tap "Delete my account and data". Your account, progress and coins are deleted straight away and cannot be brought back.
Browser data: the same button also clears web3.toys data saved in that browser. You can also clear it in your browser settings.
Anything else, or if you cannot log in: email us from the Contact page and we will delete it.

sections.title: Your rights
list: You can ask to see, correct or delete the data we hold about you, and withdraw your consent at any time, by emailing us from the Contact page.

sections.title: Sharing with project and creator pages
list: Projects, creators and web3 personalities can have a page on web3.toys. Pages about people are only ever made by those people, by logging in with their own X account.
When you earn a project's Pro badge, or join web3.toys with a creator's invite link, we ask once: share your X handle and badges with them? Nothing is shared unless you say yes.

If you say yes, that page's owner can see your display name, your X handle (if you logged in with X) and your badges for their toys and courses, and your display name may appear on their page. If you also tick the email box, they get your email address for their updates.
Owners only ever see players who said yes, and only what each player agreed to share, with the date they agreed. Everyone else is just counted, and shows as "A player" on page leaderboards.

You can stop sharing, or change the email tick, any time in My Progress, Settings. Once you stop, the owner no longer sees you. They are responsible for any copy they exported before, and must let you unsubscribe from their emails.
Page views and plays that start from a page are counted without names, so owners can see how their page is doing.

sections.title: Testers
list: If you join as a tester we store your payout wallet address, network and stablecoin choice, the date you agreed to the tester rules, your test answers, times, ratings, comments and screenshots.
Projects see your answers and screenshots in their report under a number (Tester 1, Tester 2), not your name or wallet.
Screenshots are stored privately; only you and our team can open them. Your wallet address is only seen by our team, to pay you.
Ask us at hi@web3.toys to delete your tester details. We keep payment records as the law requires.

sections.title: Age
list: Accounts and purchases are for people aged 18 or over. Anyone younger can play without an account.

sections.title: Changes
list: If we change what we collect, we will update this page and the date at the top, and ask for your agreement again when needed.
